The session\\u0027s skills root is the skills folder itself, or, when those arguments point the CLI at a directory to load from (a plugin directory, for example), that directory, which is under \\u0060.coanda/\\u0060 and holds the skills folder and nothing else. Each process of the session is told at its start which skills it has and where each one\\u0027s \\u0060SKILL.md\\u0060 is: when the daemon tells it, the persona file every process reads names each skill and the path of its \\u0060SKILL.md\\u0060 relative to the work directory; when the CLI tells it, the adapter\\u0027s remarks record the CLI version, the evidence that the CLI lists each named skill to the session, and the name it gives each one. This holds on every process of the session: the spawn, a retry\\u0027s resume, and a resume after a daemon restart, which rebuilds the session from its record. The skills root is written fresh before each of those processes, so that it holds the named skills and nothing else, whatever the session changed or added anywhere inside it, and the daemon never writes or deletes through a link the session placed, as \\u0060SessionFiles\\u0060 treats its own files. A process whose skill files cannot all be written is not started, as one whose persona file cannot be written is not; when that process is a resume, the flow run pauses with a reason naming the skill and the lever to perform the step again. A test on the adapter\\u0027s rendered arguments and files shows this for an agent naming two skills from two modules, including a resume after a file of one skill was changed and a folder was added beside them, and, when the skills root is not the skills folder, after a file was added in the skills root beside the skills folder.\u0022,\u0022A session can use only the skills its agent names. An entry whose name starts with a dot is passed over, as it is in the definitions folder. A start whose module has a skills folder holding any other loose file, a skill folder with no \\u0060SKILL.md\\u0060, or a skill folder whose name is not a plain name (letters, digits, hyphens, and underscores) is refused with a reason naming the path. A name is only ever looked up among the folders the daemon read; it is never joined onto a path.\u0022,\u0022An agent step whose agent names a skill that no module switched on for the project ships, or that two of them ship, or whose named skills include two names that differ only in letter case, pauses the flow run before its launch is recorded, so the spawn it counted stays unused and no process starts. The pause gives a reason naming the skill (and, for two modules, both modules; for two names, both names) and the lever to perform the step again, as an unknown credential profile does today.\u0022,\u0022A Claude Code session whose agent names skills has each one\\u0027s whole folder written under \\u0060.coanda/\\u0060 in the flow run\\u0027s work directory, beside the session\\u0027s other files, inside one folder that holds the session\\u0027s skills and nothing else (the session\\u0027s skills root). The skills are delivered as readable files and in no other way: the session is passed no plugin directory, no \\u0060Skill\\u0060 tool, and no other argument or setting that makes the CLI load a skill. Each process of the session is told at its start which skills it has: the persona file every process reads names each skill and the path of its \\u0060SKILL.md\\u0060 relative to the work directory, and tells the session to read a skill\\u0027s \\u0060SKILL.md\\u0060 before doing work that skill covers. This holds on every process of the session: the spawn, a retry\\u0027s resume, and a resume after a daemon restart, which rebuilds the session from its record. The skills root is written fresh before each of those processes, so that it holds the named skills and nothing else, whatever the session changed or added anywhere inside it, and the daemon never writes or deletes through a link the session placed, as \\u0060SessionFiles\\u0060 treats its own files. A process whose skill files cannot all be written is not started, as one whose persona file cannot be written is not; when that process is a resume, the flow run pauses with a reason naming the skill and the lever to perform the step again. A test on the adapter\\u0027s rendered arguments and files shows this for an agent naming two skills from two modules, including a resume after a file of one skill was changed and a folder was added beside them.\u0022,\u0022A session can use only the skills its agent names, and that holds by construction: the CLI loads no skill for it. The rendered arguments and settings document of an agent naming skills differ from those of the same agent naming none only by the tool guard\\u0027s rule for the skills root (the next criterion but one) and by the persona file\\u0027s skill lines; the \\u0060--tools\\u0060 list is unchanged, so the \\u0060Skill\\u0060 tool stays absent and no skill the CLI ships with can be invoked. A test on the rendered arguments and settings document shows this, and the adapter\\u0027s remarks name the CLI version it was confirmed against.\u0022,\u0022Reading any file of a skill a session was given is allowed by the session\\u0027s tool guard, which a test against \\u0060ToolGuard.Decide\\u0060 shows.\u0022,\u0022A session cannot change or add to the skills it was given through its file tools, and a confined session\\u0027s named skills work without loosening confinement. A no-skill session\\u0027s guard is unchanged. A confined session whose agent names skills gets them under exactly the confinement a no-skill confined session has: the same five file tools and the same path rule, the skills root being inside the work path. It loads every folder in that \\u0060skills/\\u0060 folder, not only the ones the daemon wrote.\\n- The CLI loads more than \\u0060skills/\\u0060 from a plugin directory: a manifest-less plugin directory\\u0027s \\u0060hooks/hooks.json\\u0060 ran at session start and again on \\u0060--resume\\u0060, under \\u0060--setting-sources \\u0022\\u0022\\u0060 and \\u0060--strict-mcp-config\\u0060. riteria\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:true,\u0022value\u0022:[\u0022A module\\u0027s directory may hold a \\u0060skills\\u0060 folder beside its \\u0060definitions\\u0060 folder, with one folder per skill named for the skill and holding a \\u0060SKILL.md\\u0060. The daemon reads it at start for every module whose directory it reads, whether composed or given through \\u0060DaemonOptions.ModulePaths\\u0060, and holds each skill under the module name the directory\\u0027s manifest gives. An entry of the skills folder whose name starts with a dot is passed over, as it is in the definitions folder. A start is refused, with a reason naming the path, when a module\\u0027s skills folder holds any other loose file, a skill folder with no \\u0060SKILL.md\\u0060, or a skill folder whose name is not a plain name (ASCII letters, digits, hyphens, and underscores), or when the skills folder is, or holds anywhere inside it, a symbolic link or other reparse point. A module with no skills folder starts as it does today.\u0022,\u0022When an agent step\\u0027s agent names a skill, the skill it gets is the folder of exactly that name in the skills folder of a module switched on for the parcel\\u0027s project, the module being known by the name its manifest gives. A name is only ever looked up among the folders the daemon read; it is never joined onto a path.\u0022,\u0022An agent step whose agent names a skill that no module switched on for the project ships, or that two of them ship, or whose named skills include two names that differ only in letter case, pauses the flow run before its launch is recorded, so the spawn it counted stays unused and no process starts. The pause gives a reason naming the skill (and, for two modules, both modules; for two names, both names) and the lever to perform the step again, as an unknown credential profile does today.\u0022,\u0022A Claude Code session whose agent names skills has each one\\u0027s whole folder written under \\u0060.coanda/\\u0060 in the flow run\\u0027s work directory, beside the session\\u0027s other files, inside one folder that holds the session\\u0027s skills and nothing else (the session\\u0027s skills root). The skills are delivered as readable files and in no other way: the session is passed no plugin directory, no \\u0060Skill\\u0060 tool, and no other argument or setting that makes the CLI load a skill. Each process of the session is told at its start which skills it has: the persona file every process reads names each skill and the path of its \\u0060SKILL.md\\u0060 relative to the work directory, and tells the session to read a skill\\u0027s \\u0060SKILL.md\\u0060 before doing work that skill covers. This holds on every process of the session: the spawn, a retry\\u0027s resume, and a resume after a daemon restart, which rebuilds the session from its record. The skills root is written fresh before each of those processes, so that it holds the named skills and nothing else, whatever the session changed or added anywhere inside it, and the daemon never writes or deletes through a link the session placed, as \\u0060SessionFiles\\u0060 treats its own files. A process whose skill files cannot all be written is not started, as one whose persona file cannot be written is not, and the flow run pauses with a reason naming the skill and the lever to perform the step again, whether that process is the spawn or a resume. Tests on the adapter\\u0027s rendered arguments and files show this for an agent naming two skills from two modules: at the spawn; at a retry\\u0027s resume after a file of one skill was changed, a folder was added beside the skills, and one skill\\u0027s folder was replaced by a link to a directory outside the work directory, where the resumed process finds the skills as shipped, the added folder gone, and the link\\u0027s target unchanged (the link case where the platform lets a test create a link); at the retry of a session that a new executor found from its record; and at a resume whose skills root cannot be replaced, which starts no process.\u0022,\u0022A session is given only the skills its agent names, and no session can invoke a skill through the CLI, which holds by construction. The rendered argument lists of an agent naming skills and of the same agent naming none differ only in the value of \\u0060--settings\\u0060. The two settings documents, parsed as JSON, differ only in the tool guard hook\\u0027s \\u0060args\\u0060, and \\u0060ToolGuardRules.Parse\\u0060 reads from those the same rules, except that the skill agent\\u0027s rules also carry the session\\u0027s skills root. The skill agent\\u0027s persona file is the no-skill agent\\u0027s with one block of skill lines added, as the previous criterion requires, and with that block removed the two are identical. The \\u0060--tools\\u0060 list is unchanged, so the \\u0060Skill\\u0060 tool stays absent and neither a named skill nor any skill the CLI ships with can be invoked as a skill. A test on the rendered arguments, settings document, and persona file shows this, and the adapter\\u0027s remarks name the CLI version on which the \\u0060Skill\\u0060 tool was confirmed absent when \\u0060--tools\\u0060 does not name it.\u0022,\u0022Reading any file of a skill a session was given is allowed by the session\\u0027s tool guard, which a test against \\u0060ToolGuard.Decide\\u0060 shows.\u0022,\u0022A session cannot change or add to the skills it was given through its file tools, and a confined session\\u0027s named skills work without loosening confinement. For every session whose agent names skills, confined or not, the tool guard refuses an Edit or Write whose path, in either reading the guard judges (resolved link by link, and with \\u0060.\\u0060 and \\u0060..\\u0060 collapsed by name before any link is followed, as the CLI opens it), is at or inside the session\\u0027s skills root, whether or not anything exists at it yet, so that a session cannot rewrite the instructions it is told to follow, and so that the folder is already closed to writes should a later version of the adapter let the CLI load from it. A no-skill session\\u0027s guard is unchanged. A confined session whose agent names skills gets them under exactly the confinement a no-skill confined session has: the same five file tools and the same path rule, the skills root being inside the work path. Tests in \\u0060ToolGuardTests\\u0060 and \\u0060ConfinedSessionTests\\u0060 show, for both kinds of session, three refused writes: one inside a given skill, one of a new folder beside the given skills, and one whose path reaches the skills root only through a \\u0060..\\u0060 written after a link inside the work directory. A test in \\u0060ToolGuardTests\\u0060 shows a refused write spelled relative to the work directory and, where the file system ignores letter case, one spelled in other letter case. A test shows a confined session naming a skill, with its rendered tools unchanged.\u0022,\u0022An agent that names no skill gets exactly the arguments, settings document, environment, and session files it got before this change. Every existing expectation in \\u0060ClaudeCodeExecutorTests\\u0060, \\u0060ConfinedSessionTests\\u0060, and \\u0060ToolGuardTests\\u0060 passes unchanged, and a test shows that a no-skill agent\\u0027s guard hook arguments carry no skills root and its persona file names no skill.\u0022,\u0022The scripted executor\\u0027s record of a spawn names each skill the session was given, so a test can assert on it without a real session.\u0022,\u0022No event, definition content, or content hash changes: every stored agent reads and hashes as it does today.\u0022,\u0022\\u0060docs/design/design.md\\u0060 says where a module keeps its skills, how an agent\\u0027s named skill is resolved, and what happens when it cannot be, in place of the sentence in section 9 that skills stay vendor-native repo files referenced by name; it says how a session receives its named skills where section 10 says the adapter renders skills to tier paths; and it names the skills folder where sections 14.2 and 14.8 list what a module brings and what its artifact holds. \\u0060docs/node-configuration.md\\u0060 says, under \\u0022How a Claude Code session runs\\u0022, what a session whose agent names skills receives and where its skill files are written; under \\u0022What a session\\u0027s tools cannot reach\\u0022, that an Edit or Write into the session\\u0027s skills root is refused; and under \\u0022What a confined session may reach\\u0022, what a confined session naming skills gets.
